display.prose: Only two premises bear on the query. The register entries (p0–p3, p5–p11, p13–p28) are unary facts about Ben and say nothing about trust, and Ada almost following Ben (p12) is irrelevant too. Premise p29 concerns respect. As formalized here, it says there is a person who respects no one. Call that person x0. Premise p4 links respect and trust. As formalized here, whenever a person y trusts x, x respects y. So every trust link is paired with a respect link running the opposite way. Now apply p4 to x0. Suppose some person y trusted x0. Then by p4, x0 would respect y. But p29 says x0 respects no one. So no person trusts x0. It follows that there is a person whom nobody trusts. That is exactly the query: it is not the case that everyone is trusted by someone. The deduction uses only p4 and p29, and the checker certifies it. The answer is True.
